research.topic: wires-and-connections: how a Satisfactory logic (redstone-like) mod can connect its elements
research.summary:
Vanilla already has a generic wire/circuit layer, and one third-party library shows it can host a second network type. FicsIt-Networks and Circuitry show the alternatives.

(1) At SDK d2162c99 (identical to SML master on 2026-10-13) both UFGCircuitConnectionComponent and AFGBuildableWire carry a mCircuitType, and the headers say "power or logic". UFGCircuit is abstract; AFGWireHologram filters connectors by circuit type. KMods' published library "KMods Library - Code" (MIT source, SML ^3.12.0) builds a whole second network this way: custom circuit, connector, wire and wire hologram. It derives from UFGPowerCircuit and fakes power production. Every SDK .cpp is an auto-generated stub, so the runtime behaviour of a direct UFGCircuit subclass (ticking via circuit groups, split, save, uninstall) is UNVERIFIED and needs a spike on the owner's PC. Vanilla circuits give connected-component membership (a shared bus), not directed per-wire signals; gates need separate input and output circuits.

(2) FicsIt-Networks (GPL-3.0) reuses none of it. It has its own AFINNetworkCircuit actor with a recursive DFS over IFINNetworkCircuitNode, an AFINNetworkCable derived from AFGBuildable, and its own hologram. Signals go through a sender-to-listener subsystem, not along cables.

(3) Circuitry/FicsitWiremod (no licence file) stores per-input UObject* + FName pull links, spline wire actors, per-gate Tick and RCOs. It already targets SML ^3.12.0 and game >=502094, so it is a design-only reference and a niche overlap. Other precedents: DaisyChainEverything mutates mMaxNumConnectionLinks; Cable Choices Plus subclasses AFGBuildableWire in C++; SmartWirelessLighting keeps a replicated link list in a hub.

(4) Alternatives are hidden connections (code-only, SaveGame but not Replicated), actor-reference link tools (client edits need an RCO), numeric channels (Factorio precedent; no SMR example found) and adjacency (Minecraft).

(5) Native defaults are 10000 cm wire length and 1 link per connector. The wiki gives poles 4/7/10 links and wires 100 m/300 m. No published wire or circuit cap and no benchmark was found, only code hints such as "full rebuild (slow)".

Recommendation: spike option A on the PC; fall back to a FIN-style own graph; add hidden-connection or channel wireless and an RCO-backed link tool.

claims.statement: Vanilla wires and connectors are typed by a per-class circuit type. UFGCircuitConnectionComponent and AFGBuildableWire each have a mCircuitType (TSubclassOf<UFGCircuit>, EditDefaultsOnly), the comments name 'logic' as an intended circuit type, and connecting two different types is declared illegal. The class hierarchy is UFGConnectionComponent -> UFGCircuitConnectionComponent -> UFGPowerConnectionComponent; the power connector's stub constructor sets mCircuitType = UFGPowerCircuit. SML master HEAD equals the owner's pinned commit d2162c99 ('Update headers to CL502094', 2026-08-11), so main and the pin agree. Design intent only; the runtime is closed source (see c4).

evidence.quote: E.g. power connections can belong to power circuits and logic connection can belong to logic circuits.
Note that it is illegal to try to connect two connections with different types.
Circuit type this wire is used for. Can only be one, e.g. power or logic.

claims.statement: A published third-party library already implements a complete second network type on top of the vanilla circuit machinery, all in C++. 'KMods Library - Code' (SMR KPrivateCodeLib 2026.3.514, 2026-08-30, SML ^3.12.0, game >=491125, ~504k downloads, source under MIT) defines UKPCLNetwork derived from UFGPowerCircuit, UKPCLNetworkConnectionComponent derived from UFGPowerConnectionComponent with mCircuitType = UKPCLNetwork, AKPCLNetworkCable derived from AFGBuildableWire (UCLASS Abstract, so a Blueprint child is needed), and AKPCLNetworkCableHologram derived from AFGWireHologram. Members are found via AFGCircuitSubsystem::FindCircuit(GetCircuitID()). Caveat: it derives from the POWER circuit and fakes power production (KFaxitFakePowerProduced = 50000000.f) and sets mHasPower/fuse flags each tick. That suggests a clean UFGCircuit subclass was not used or not sufficient. I did not establish which released mod uses this network at runtime.

claims.statement: Vanilla circuits compute connected-component membership (a shared bus), not directed per-wire signals. The header states A and B are known to be connected but not whether a wire joins them directly. The wire is just an 'edge in a circuit graph'. A bridge or switch building joins two circuits into one when active. A redstone-like gate therefore needs one connector on an input circuit and a different connector on an output circuit, with its own evaluation step (design inference, not in the sources).

evidence.quote: We can say that A and B are connected (indirectly or directly) but not if there is a wire directly between A and B.
This is an edge in a circuit graph.
Building that connects two circuits, allowing them to act as one single circuit. Intended as base for switches and similar buildings.

claims.statement: UNVERIFIED: whether a non-power circuit type works end to end in the game binary. All SML FactoryGame .cpp files are auto-generated empty stubs (e.g. AFGCircuitSubsystem::Get returns nullptr), so ticking, splitting, replication and save of a custom circuit cannot be checked from source. Hints that it is not trivial: UFGCircuit::SplitCircuit and CreateCircuitGroup default to nullptr; 'Circuit groups are responsible for ticking the circuits in them' (the power group overrides PushCircuit, PreTick/TickCircuitGroup, VisitCircuitBridge); AFGBuildableCircuitBridge has a power-group-specific AcceptCircuitGroup overload; the only existing non-vanilla example (c2) derives from UFGPowerCircuit and fakes power. Among headers named *Circuit*, only FGPowerCircuit.h declares a UFGCircuit subclass. I searched the web and GitHub for a direct UFGCircuit subclass and found none. Needs a spike on the owner's PC (go/no-go: ticks on a dedicated server, replicates to a client, survives save/load, loads after the mod is removed).

claims.statement: FicsIt-Networks does NOT reuse UFGCircuit/AFGBuildableWire. It has its own graph: AFINNetworkCircuit (an AActor that caches the Nodes array, rebuilt by recursive DFS from any node via the IFINNetworkCircuitNode::GetConnected interface), UFINNetworkConnectionComponent (a USceneComponent node with MaxCables, ConnectedCables and hidden ConnectedNodes), and AFINNetworkCable derived from AFGBuildable (Connector1/Connector2 are SaveGame + Replicated). Connect/disconnect merges or splits circuits through static ConnectNodes/DisconnectNodes. The graph is rebuilt from the saved cables on load (cable BeginPlay calls ConnectConnectors). The files cited are identical on master v1.2.0 (789c32f, the published release) and on the development branch (e588fab, 1.3.0); I diffed them, and only minor differences exist in ConnectionComponent.cpp, Cable.cpp and SignalSubsystem.

claims.statement: Circuitry (SMR FicsitWiremod, Scordium/FicsitWiremod) uses a pull-based model, not circuits. Each gate (AFGWiremodBuildable derived from AFGBuildable) stores InputConnections, an array of FConnectionData {UObject* Object, FName FunctionName, wire colour/points}, marked SaveGame + Replicated. Values are read by reflection from the source object. The visible wire is a separate plain AActor with spline meshes (AConnectionWireBase, replicated AssignedConnection). Every gate ticks (ServerProcess on authority, ClientProcess everywhere) with NetDormancy DORM_Never. It is published (v14.1.63, 2026-09-26, ~195k downloads) for SML ^3.12.0 and game >=502094, the owner's exact build, and its Content/ has hundreds of gate assets. The GitHub API reports license null and the repo root has no LICENSE file, so the code is design-only reference, not reusable. It overlaps the 'logic gates for Satisfactory' niche; the product must differentiate.

claims.statement: In multiplayer, a client cannot call server code on arbitrary objects; link create/edit/delete from a client link tool must go through a Remote Call Object (one per player controller, owned by that controller). Multicast must not be used from RCOs. Both shipped logic/network mods do this: Circuitry exposes ConnectWiremodObject/ResetConnections as Reliable Server RPCs on a UFGRemoteCallObject subclass; FIN has UFINWirelessRCO. A custom vanilla-style wire built with the build gun does not need an RCO (the build gun already constructs on the server), but any numeric-channel or link-tool UI does.

claims.statement: Vanilla has a code-only link inside the circuit machinery: 'hidden connections'. AddHiddenConnection/RemoveHiddenConnection/HasHiddenConnection are BlueprintCallable; one of the two connectors must be flagged hidden (mIsHiddenConnection); both ends and their circuits get connected. mHiddenConnections is SaveGame but NOT Replicated (unlike mWires and mCircuitID). Vanilla uses it for powered walls and rail power; the official docs confirm hidden connections exist. This is the natural primitive for wireless or snapped links on the vanilla circuit layer. The client only learns membership via the replicated mCircuitID.

evidence.quote: Add a hidden connection to another connection component. One of the connections must be hidden for this to be valid.
This connection is hidden and can only be connected through the code. E.g. powered walls have a hidden connection all machines connect to.
The non-wired (if this or the other is hidden) connections to this.
It manages cable connections and hidden connections from other connection components to itself. It f.e. limits the number of cables you can attach to it.

claims.statement: Vanilla wire building flow (hologram): AFGWireHologram is a multi-step AFGBuildableHologram that holds two connector pointers and finds the nearest connector via FindOverlappingCircuitConnectionComponent filtered by compatible circuit type. It can auto-spawn a child pole through mDefaultPowerPoleRecipe and mDefaultPowerPoleWallRecipe, which a non-power wire must null. Length and cost come from the wire class (mMaxLength cm, mMaxPowerTowerLength, mLengthPerCost). AFGBuildableWire::Connect(first, second) is public. Disqualifiers such as UFGCDWireTooLong, UFGCDWireTooManyConnections and UFGCDWireSnap exist. FIN wrote its own hologram on AFGBuildableHologram; KMods subclassed AFGWireHologram (c2).

claims.statement: Gameplay numbers (secondary, community-edited official wiki): Power Line max length 100 m (Power Pole) and 300 m (Power Tower, one cable per 25 m extra); most buildings accept one line, storages and lights two, poles 4/7/10 by mark; no capacity limit on lines. Official Steam announcement for Update 1.2 confirms the 'Daisy chaining' MAM unlock (2 power connections per building, building-to-building flow).

evidence.quote: The maximum length of a Power Line is 100 meters (12.5 Foundation lengths) for the Power Pole and 300 meters (37,5 Foundation lengths) for the Power Tower
Most buildings may only have one Power Line connected to it, Power Storages and Lights can have two; Power Poles four, seven or ten (based on the mark).
This new MAM Unlock allows 2 power connections to be made to the same building and lets you connect buildings to each other allowing power to flow from building to building

claims.statement: Daisy Chain Everything (SMR DaisyChainEverything 1.2.0, game >=502094, repo mklierman/SatisfactoryMods, GPL-3.0) raises the per-connector link cap at runtime by writing UFGPowerConnectionComponent::mMaxNumConnectionLinks on every AFGBuildable via an SML native hook on BeginPlay. It needs an AccessTransformers.ini friend declaration because the member is not public. The link cap is therefore a plain per-instance property, not a hard engine limit, and SML hooks and access transformers are the standard way to poke vanilla internals.

claims.statement: Cable Choices Plus (SMR AB_CableMod 1.1.9, 2026-10-12, ~112k downloads; no LICENSE file) subclasses AFGBuildableWire in C++ (AABBuildablePowerline, with an empty constructor and Blueprint children carrying the data) and hooks AFGBuildableWire::UpdateWireInstanceMesh with SML's SUBSCRIBE_METHOD_AFTER. So C++ wire subclasses plus hooks on wire internals are viable in a shipped mod. Note its 1.1.9 requires game >=513885, which is newer than the owner's CL 502094.

claims.statement: Hard-won lessons on spawning wires from code (SmartFoundations, majormer, licence NOASSERTION/all-rights-reserved header): wires should be direct-spawned and then Connect()ed after both ends exist, not replayed from holograms (that produced unconnected 'zombie' wires in multiplayer); unconnected wires are destroyed by the game; a failed Connect can leave a dead entry in the connector's SaveGame wire list, so use Dismantle rather than Destroy; wires spanning a Blueprint Designer boundary need the designer stamped before BeginPlay. A logic wire built from code must follow these rules.

claims.statement: Blueprint Designer interaction is a known pitfall for any custom wire: Coffee Stain fixed 'circuits from outside the Blueprint Designer' connecting to inside, and FIN's cable hologram adds the vanilla UFGCDDesignerWorldCommingling disqualifier when the two ends are on different sides of a designer. A logic wire must replicate that check.

evidence.quote: Fixed Double Wall Outlet allowing circuits from outside the Blueprint Designer to connect to those inside of it

claims.statement: FIN signals are not propagated along cables. The network graph only defines reachability and addressing (GUID + nick). Signals are events: AFINSignalSubsystem keeps a SaveGame map of sender object -> listener traces and BroadcastSignal calls each listener's HandleSignal; hooks are attached to the sender via the reflection hook subsystem. FIN's own docs describe the network as cables joining components ('You can build a network by simply connecting a network cable...'). An event-driven design is cheap but cannot express per-wire redstone-style levels.

claims.statement: FIN wireless is not wire-free logic. A Wireless Access Point must sit on a powered Radar Tower and its range equals the tower's discovery range; the AP is a network connector that bridges separate cable networks, so FIN keeps the cable graph as the model and layers wireless on top (AFINWirelessSubsystem recomputes AP/tower topology).

claims.statement: Link-by-reference precedents. Circuitry's radio receiver stores a replicated, saved direct actor reference to its transmitter (no channel numbers) and sets it from the UI, clipboard or RCO. SmartWirelessLighting (GPL-3.0) derives from the vanilla lights control panel and keeps a replicated array of light connections on the hub 'without the need for spaghetti cables'. Vanilla's AFGBuildableControlPanelHost collects buildables on a downstream power connection, so vanilla already lets one hub drive devices over a power-circuit link.

claims.statement: Replication and save of stored links. Unreal replicates a UObject* property as a NetGUID, but only for replicated actors, stably named non-replicated actors, replicated components, stably named components and similar objects. Vanilla connectors set bNetAddressable = true and replicate mWires; FIN's cable and Circuitry's FConnectionData keep their endpoint pointers as SaveGame properties, so saving actor references works in shipped mods. FIN additionally prunes dead sender/listener entries in PreSaveGame (Cleanup), and SmartFoundations documents dead entries in a SaveGame wire list asserting after reload, so dangling-reference cleanup is mandatory.

claims.statement: Code-level performance hints for the vanilla circuit system (no measurements): MarkForFullRebuild is documented '(slow)'; many connect/disconnect calls in one frame collapse into one rebuild; the subsystem ticks every frame (TickInterval 0.0) on dedicated servers; the whole circuit array is replicated to clients as a duplicate array; replication of power stats is switched off when nobody looks at a circuit ('Hax'); Coffee Stain left an @optimize note on always-replicated circuit state. KMods parallelises member scanning when a circuit has more than 7 power infos (KFaxitCircuitParallelGroups = 7), a sign that large circuit rebuilds were costly for them (my inference).

claims.statement: FIN's graph costs, from code: each circuit is a replicated actor with bAlwaysRelevant and DORM_Awake and a replicated Nodes array; recalculation is a recursive DFS with a recursive reachability check that the code itself marks 'slow!'. Circuitry gates tick every frame with DORM_Never (c6). These are structural costs; no benchmark was found for either.

claims.statement: Official patch notes (Coffee Stain, via the Steam News API) contain no numeric limit on wires or circuits. They mention 'Optimized Power Lines' (Update 4) and 'Potential fix for a crash in the Circuit Subsystem' (v1.0.0.5), which shows the subsystem has had stability work but gives no cliff.

claims.statement: NOT FOUND: any published practical limit for the number of wires, connectors or circuits per world, or any benchmark of vanilla circuit rebuild cost. Tried: SDK headers and stub constructors, docs.ficsit.app (the PowerNetwork page is a stub that admits 'We currently don't really know how the power network works'), the full Steam news feed (300 items), wiki.gg and the Fandom wiki (402), a hosting-company blog (timeout), and GitHub code search. A budget has to be measured on the owner's dedicated server (see openQuestions).

claims.statement: Numeric-channel wireless: Factorio's radar 'Universe Mode' broadcasts to a selectable channel and every radar on the same channel receives it. No Satisfactory mod with numeric channels or frequencies was found, only actor-reference links (c19) or powered-radar-tower wireless (c18). The SMR 'Wireless Power' mod (2022, SML ^3.2.0, no source) was not inspected. So a channel registry is feasible in principle (a replicated ModSubsystem mapping int -> members) but has no in-game precedent evidence.

evidence.quote: Radars will transmit any signals passed to it to a particular selectable channel. The signal will be picked up by all other radars set to the same channel

claims.statement: Design references from the games the owner cited: Factorio circuit networks are shared buses (devices on a wire sum all signals, same-colour wires merge networks, wires can run across power poles); Minecraft redstone dust is adjacency-based with attenuation (transmits up to 15 blocks, weaker signals travel less). Vanilla Satisfactory circuits resemble the Factorio bus model (c3), not the Minecraft adjacency model.

evidence.quote: A circuit network consists only of those devices connected together with the same color wire.
Receiving devices sum all signals from each wire connected to them, even red and green wires.
Redstone wire is a non-solid block that can transmit a redstone power signal up to 15 blocks in distance; signal strengths below 15 have reduced distance.

claims.statement: Editor-asset needs (matters because this session has no Unreal): the logic classes (circuit, connector, wire, hologram, gate logic) can be written as C++ text, as KMods did. But the buildable chain still needs Content: KMods' cable class is UCLASS(Abstract) (needs a Blueprint child), FIN loads its cable descriptor from a Content path (Desc_NetworkCable), and Circuitry ships its gates as hundreds of .uasset files (uplugin CanContainContent true). The owner's existing CompanionPresence is C++-only (no Content). Whether descriptors, recipes and meshes can be avoided by reusing vanilla assets by path (SmartFoundations loads Build_PowerLine by path) or by ContentLib was not established.

openQuestions: SPIKE on the owner's PC (decides option A vs B): does a direct UFGCircuit subclass (not UFGPowerCircuit) get ticked, replicated to clients and saved? KMods avoids it by faking power. Check what ticks a circuit with no circuit group, how SplitCircuit=nullptr behaves, and whether a save loads after the mod is removed (circuit objects are SaveGame).

Does AFGWireHologram work unmodified for a non-power circuit type? Its mCircuitType is a private UPROPERTY() and the auto-pole recipes must be nulled. KMods subclassed it, but its Blueprint defaults were not examined.
Which released mod, if any, runs the KMods network at runtime? Only source and SMR library metadata were checked, so runtime viability of c2 is not independently confirmed.

Minimum editor assets for a buildable wire and connector (descriptor, recipe, mesh, Blueprint child of an abstract C++ wire, UMG for channel entry). Can vanilla assets by path or ContentLib avoid the editor? Not researched.

Measured limits: build a test save with N wires and M gates (for example 1k/5k/10k wires) on a dedicated server and record tick time, rebuild hitch on dismantle, and replication bandwidth. No published limit exists (c24).

Product overlap with Circuitry (FicsitWiremod), which already covers logic gates, sensors and radio on SML ^3.12.0 / >=502094. Decide the differentiator (physical redstone-style bus wires, latches/clocks, FRM sensors) or interoperate. Circuitry has no licence, so no code reuse.

SMR lists Cable Choices Plus 1.1.9 (2026-10-12) with game_version >=513885, newer than the owner's CL 502094. Confirm whether a newer public or experimental game build exists and whether the SDK pin needs bumping.

Hidden connections are SaveGame but not Replicated: confirm that clients see correct circuit membership (via the replicated mCircuitID) for hidden-connection links, or whether a replicated mirror list is needed.

Interaction with vanilla flows: Blueprint Designer boundaries, wire upgrade and split (TryUpgrade), zooping and dismantle refund (GetDismantleRefundReturnsMultiplier) must be handled for a custom wire.
Licence choice for the new mod: GPL-3.0 if any FIN or DaisyChainEverything code is copied; MIT if only KMods code is reused (check assets); Circuitry and Cable Choices are design-only.

MATRIX G | Adjacency or socket snapping (Minecraft-like, breadboard grid) | Impl: hologram snapping code; Circuitry breadboard stores grid cells as SaveGame [V c6 repo] | UX: no cables, strong spatial constraint, limits layouts [S c26] | MP: only building placement replicates [U] | Save: building positions only [U] | Perf: neighbour query at build time [U] | Evidence: Minecraft adjacency model [V c26]; weakest fit for a big factory.

RECOMMENDED PATH: run a time-boxed spike of option A on the owner's PC first. Go/no-go tests: custom UFGCircuit subclass ticks on a dedicated server, replicates to a client, survives save/load and loads after the mod is removed, and a hologram with auto-pole recipes nulled builds and upgrades. If it fails, drop to a FIN-style own graph (B), keeping the same gameplay model. Do not copy Circuitry's pull model.

GATE MODEL (design inference [U]): treat each logic circuit as a shared bus carrying a value (Factorio-style sum or OR). A gate is a building with an input connector on one circuit and an output connector on another, evaluated once per tick with a one-tick delay. This avoids evaluation-order loops, fits vanilla's membership semantics (c3) and gives latches and clocks naturally.

WIRELESS AND UI: add wire-free links through hidden connections (D) or a replicated channel registry (E), and a link tool only where cables are impractical. Every client-side edit goes through an RCO (c7). Cap per-world counts in config until measured, since there is no known limit (c24).

VPS vs PC split: write and unit-test pure logic here as plain C++ (circuit graph, gate truth tables, tick scheduler, channel registry) with g++ and no Unreal; this is feasible only for code that does not include FactoryGame headers [U]. Anything touching UFGCircuit, holograms, descriptors, recipes, meshes, UMG or packaging needs the owner's PC with UE 5.6.1-css-83 and Alpakit.
LICENCE: choose MIT or GPL-3.0 deliberately. Reuse only KMods (MIT source) or write clean-room; any FIN or DaisyChainEverything code forces GPL-3.0; Circuitry and Cable Choices are design-only.

verdicts.corrected: In multiplayer, client-to-server calls must go through an RCO (one per player controller, owned by it); Multicast must not be used from RCOs. Circuitry uses a UFGRemoteCallObject subclass (UWiremodRemoteCalls) with Reliable Server RPCs, including ConnectWiremodObject and ResetConnections, for its link tool. FIN does NOT use an RCO for linking: UFINWirelessRCO only subscribes a client UI to wireless-access-point connection data. FIN also has RCOs for its Computer and Lua UIs. The point that build-gun-placed wires need no RCO is the author's inference; no source was cited for it.
verdicts.note: The 2 docs.ficsit.app/Multiplayer.html quotes are verbatim, and the page says RPCs only work on objects (transitively) owned by the connection. WiremodRemoteCalls.h is verbatim: 'UCLASS(Abstract, Blueprintable) class FICSITWIREMOD_API UWiremodRemoteCalls : public UFGRemoteCallObject' with 'UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Reliable, Server)' on ConnectWiremodObject and ResetConnections. The FINWirelessRCO.h quote is verbatim, but its own comment reads 'RCO used to trigger updates on the server, in order to recalculate the currently displayed radar towers & WAP'. So 'Both shipped logic/network mods do this' (for link create/edit/delete) holds only for Circuitry. In FIN's circuit module the cable path (AFINNetworkCable, hologram) contains no RCO, which is consistent with the build-gun inference but does not prove it.

verdicts.corrected: Membership-not-direction and the three quotes are confirmed. Imprecise part: a bridge/switch does not merge two circuits into one. The circuits keep separate IDs (AFGBuildableCircuitBridge exposes GetCircuitID0/GetCircuitID1) and active bridges merge them at circuit-GROUP level. Groups exist only on the server; clients compare group IDs. The gate-design inference (separate input and output circuits plus a custom evaluation step) still holds, but a custom group type would be needed (UFGCircuit::CreateCircuitGroup defaults to nullptr).
verdicts.note: FGPowerCircuit.h: "A circuit group is a grouping of circuits connected by switches. When I switch is turned on the circuits on both sides are grouped together. This is to avoid traversing the circuit connections and rebuilding the circuits when a switch is flipped." and "Groups only exist on the server, on the client you can compare group IDs". FGCircuitSubsystem.h: bridges "work as delimiters of circuits"; if on, not delimiters of circuit groups. FGBuildableCircuitSwitch.h: "allowing them to act as one single circuit when the switch is turned on." Quotes in the claim (FGCircuit.h, FGBuildableWire.h, FGBuildableCircuitBridge.h) are verbatim.

Open status confirmed; my refutation attempts found no proof either way. GitHub-wide code search ("public UFGCircuit", "public UFGPowerCircuit") returned only header mirrors plus KMods; docs.ficsit.app has no circuit-type page (PowerNetwork.html describes only power circuits). Mixed hints: subsystem CreateCircuit(TSubclassOf<UFGCircuit>), mReplicatedCircuits (TArray<UFGCircuit>) and the wire hologram circuit-type filter are generic, which favours feasibility. Against: even the power-derived KMods route needed runtime hooks and its consumers say multiplayer is untested. verdicts.corrected: Core holds: client-to-server link/edit calls need an RCO, Multicast is forbidden in RCOs, Circuitry does this, and the build gun already constructs on the server so a build-gun wire needs no RCO. Overgeneralised: 'both mods do this'. FIN's three RCOs (UFINWirelessRCO, UFINComputerRCO, UFINLuaRCO) serve wireless-AP subscription, computer/GPU input, SetNick etc. and are not used to create links; FIN cables are build-gun buildables.

Verbatim: "Add a hidden connection to another connection component. One of the connections must be hidden for this to be valid." mHiddenConnections is UPROPERTY(VisibleAnywhere, SaveGame) with no Replicated. The stub GetLifetimeReplicatedProps lists only mWires, mNumWiresConnected and mCircuitID. The docs page says "It manages cable connections and hidden connections" and lists "The list of hidden connections (f.e. train rails)". Extra vanilla users found: FGBuildableElevator.h calls RemoveHiddenConnection for floor stops, a decompiled Build_PowerPoleWallDouble BP calls PowerConnection1->AddHiddenConnection(PowerConnection2) (Archengius/BPPseudoCodeGen), and FGRailroadSubsystem.h mentions a "station's hidden power connection".
